bull_bear.body:
- **Net debt ≈ zero / net cash** despite Agastya ₹850 cr loan; debt-equity & debt-EBITDA "very healthy" — comfortable carrying some debt.
- Surplus cash priority: **(1) acquire growth assets (Anant via internal accruals to large extent), (2) debt reduction** with leftover.
- No dividend discussion on call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Earnings lumpiness:** dry-docks (Paladin + Diamond in Q4; 3 more — Seamec III/Princess/Glorious — in FY27, but in monsoon to limit disruption), contract changeovers, vessel off-hire.
- **Vessel/machinery breakdown risk** (24/7 ops; last-quarter breakdown addressed, no client penalty, but recurring breakdowns would be the real concern; not insured).
- **Offshore-capex / oil-price cyclicality**; ONGC dependence (single dominant customer ecosystem).
- **Related-party / HAL Offshore concentration** (needs ONGC + shareholder approvals — Anant delayed ~1 year over RPT-limit/ONGC approvals).
- **Aging fleet:** DG Shipping age-norms currently exempt DSVs, but prudent recycle-vs-operate decisions ahead.
- One-off dependence (Goodman ₹22 cr+) inflates the optical Q3 base.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: - Confident/upbeat — "landmark quarter," "best ever," "strongest quarter to date," "FY27 a year of growth." Disciplined messaging: repeatedly steers investors to YEARLY view; transparent about Goodman one-off and Q4 dry-dock drag.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- The **Goodman vessel (₹22 cr+)** is structurally interesting: management is deliberately **migrating HAL Offshore's contracts/vessels into Seamec** (renting vessels from parent at marginal cost), so the listed entity captures economics that historically sat in the parent — a recurring value-transfer lever, even if this specific contract was a one-off.
- **No insurance on high-value charters** — breakdown risk is self-priced into day-rates; a structural margin/risk feature, not a gap.
- Anant's lower **$45k** rate vs Swordfish **$75k** is spec/scope/risk-driven (newer ≠ pricier) — refutes naive "new vessel = premium rate."
- OALP-VIII / new ONGC blocks are a **4–6 year** optionality, not a near-term catalyst.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt position has swung from Rs 48 Cr (FY24) to net cash of -Rs 287 Cr by YTD FY27, alongside a reduction in gross debt, reflecting a strengthening balance sheet.
- Return on Capital Employed improved from 10% (FY24) to 20% (YTD FY27) and Return on Equity from 13% to 19% over the same period, per the deck's balance sheet highlights.
- Stated capital allocation philosophy: focus on demand-backed vessel acquisitions, with a strong balance sheet supporting future expansion opportunities rather than aggressive leverage.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Described as a formidable player in the DSV sector in India, backed by fleet strength of diverse nature such as MSV, OSV and Barge
- Diversified fleet composition - 'The combination of Fleets of diversed nature has strengthened the Company's position in different area'
- Long-term charter contracts with ONGC running to 2028 and 2029, giving multi-year deployment visibility
- Presence prominently both in India and overseas, allowing redeployment across markets
- Assessed under the Tonnage Tax Scheme, giving a lower effective tax burden than normal corporate tax rates
- Promoter/holding company HAL Offshore Limited provides a channel to ONGC charter contracts
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical disruption to overseas deployment and drydock access — The MD&A states the adverse geo-political situation is a concern and threat for overseas deployment and for availing drydock services, and that this has been experienced by the Company. Strait of Hormuz closure and Middle East conflict directly interrupted vessel movement and drydocking.
- Single-segment concentration in the offshore business — The business segment for the Company during the year under review has been the offshore segment in the domestic market, so earnings depend entirely on offshore oil and gas activity with no diversifying segment.
- Customer concentration on ONGC, largely routed through the holding company — SEAMEC PALADIN, SEAMEC AGASTYA, SEAMEC II and SEAMEC DIAMOND are all engaged with ONGC, with several of those contracts held through HAL Offshore Limited, the holding company - concentrating both counterparty and related-party exposure.
- Charter renewal and contract roll-off risk — Deployment is tied to a small number of dated charters - SEAMEC II runs only till August 2026, the SWORDFISH charter is two years from August 2025 and the GLORIOUS barge charter is 150 days from November 2025 - so revenue continuity depends on rewinning work as each expires.
- Vessel downtime from statutory drydocking — Drydocking takes revenue-earning assets off hire and raises depreciation; SEAMEC III and SEAMEC PRINCESS are scheduled for drydock in June and August 2026, and drydocking of Sea Diamond and Agastya already raised depreciation in FY 2025-26.
- Exposure to oil and gas capital-spending and crude price cycles — The Chairman notes major challenges ranging from low crude oil prices to supply chain pressures, and the industry outlook is built on a baseline of moderate oil prices averaging USD 65 - USD 85 per barrel; offshore support demand follows operator upstream spending.
- Workforce and skilled-manpower constraint — The Chairman's message states that workforce strategy has emerged as a material business risk and flags workforce constraint as a sector-wide challenge; the MD&A notes offshore projects depend on skilled professionals including drilling engineers and ROV operators.
- Structural technology shift toward AUV/ROV and digitalisation of the value chain — The MD&A notes that in India more emphasis is being given to Automation Underwater Vehicles and Remotely Operated Vehicles, and that operators are accelerating digitisation - a conventional-vessel fleet risks obsolescence without matching investment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **IMR contracts = higher-margin, full-year deployment (incl. monsoon), no off-hire** — strategic preference; all new high-value assets assumed/deployed on IMR (only profitable that way).
- **EPC = 2 older-vintage vessels** (zero book value); don't work in monsoon; lower revenue but any business improves ROC/ROE/bottom line since assets are at ₹0.
- Target IMR/EPC mix over 3–5 yrs: directionally toward IMR; no hard ratio given.
business.title: Segment (vessel charter / IMR vs EPC)

business.body:
- ✅ India upstream/offshore capex push, ONGC OALP-VIII & ONGC-RIL offshore resource-sharing → long-dated demand for DSV/IMR vessels (Seamec, HAL-linked operators).
- ⭐ DG Shipping age-norm exemption for DSVs → incumbents with older DSV fleets (Seamec) retain operating runway.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

business.body:
- Describes itself as 'a formidable player in offshore shipping backed by India's largest fleet of multi-support vessels', a leading provider of specialised engineering services (subsea and marine operations) to the offshore oil & gas industry.
- Long operating history with ONGC and international oil majors; clientele includes ONGC, L&T, POSH, Safeen Al Behar, Zamil Offshore, Clipper Petroleum, Lamprell Energy, Mermaid, Eagle Bulk Shipping and Westfield Energy. High entry barriers from specialised equipment and certification requirements.
- Part of the MMG Group since HAL Offshore acquired the company from the erstwhile Technip India group in 2014; promoter holding ~72.72%.
- Cites strong MMG parentage as strengthening financial position and market reputation, with technical expertise and financial strength positioning it favourably in the tendering process.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired Aarey Organic Industries Private Limited to carry out manufacturing, selling, importing, exporting and distributing various types of chemicals — a diversification outside the core marine/offshore business.
- [Policy Tailwind] Government approved the 'Samudra Manthan' National Offshore Exploration Scheme with a total outlay of ₹84,084 crore through FY2030-31, offering financial assistance of up to 50% of eligible exploration costs — a structural demand driver for offshore service providers like SEAMEC.
- [Industry Demand] ONGC floated offshore vessel tenders worth ₹1,000+ crore under 'Make in India'; India's offshore facilities pipeline includes 25 installations and 1,000+ km of subsea pipelines over the next three years.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: SEAMEC owns and charters out multi support vessels, an offshore support vessel and a barge that provide diving, subsea, repair, maintenance and construction support to offshore oil and gas operators. The Company's business segment during the year under review has been the offshore segment in the domestic market, with vessels also deployed overseas. Vessels are chartered to clients such as ONGC (in part through holding company HAL Offshore Limited), L&T and Middle East operators, and the Company also provides operation and management services for third-party owned vessels.

latest_quarter.body:
- ~45% EBITDA margin (₹150 cr on ₹331 cr consol) — IMR-mix + record utilization + Goodman one-off.
- Risk/breakdown contingency **priced into day-rates** (not insured — high-value charter premiums prohibitive); a margin buffer kept for breakdowns.
- IMR > EPC on margin; zero-book EPC vessels are pure margin accretion when working.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q3 FY26 (this call):** Record qtr — consol rev ₹331 cr (+138% YoY), EBITDA ₹150 cr, PAT ₹100 cr (vs ₹3 cr loss YoY); highest-ever deployment. Day-rates: Swordfish ~$75k, Anant ~$45k. Agastya (5-yr, $23m, ₹850 cr/8yr debt) deployed. Anant acquisition to close Q4, deploy Q1FY27 (50:50 funding). Goodman one-off +₹22 cr+. Net cash. Q4 guided softer (Paladin + Diamond dry-docks). ₹1,000 cr DG Shipping MoU for 1+ vessels over 2–3 yrs. FY27 = growth year (Swordfish full year). Manage to yearly, not quarterly.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Day-rate outlook:** Rates at highs; management expects them to remain **steady/sustained** "for some more time" — no normalization signalled near-term.
- **Utilization outlook:** Record deployment; aiming for more **IMR (inspection-maintenance-repair) contracts** which give full-year (incl. monsoon) deployment vs EPC (no monsoon work) to "streamline the quarters."
- **Fleet additions:** **Swordfish full-year contribution in FY27** (only part-year in FY26); **Agastya** now deployed; **Anant acquisition to close within FY26 (Q4), deployed Q1 FY27** with revenue from then.
- **Order/contract inflow:** Strategy to migrate new HAL Offshore contracts into Seamec (grow Seamec's share; HAL book to deplete as contracts expire).
- **FY27 = a "year of GROWTH"** (Swordfish full year + Agastya + Anant), per management — explicitly NOT a consolidation year.
- Management repeatedly: **judge performance YEAR-over-YEAR, not quarter-over-quarter** (dry-docks/changeovers cause lumpiness).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- No consolidated order-book ₹ figure disclosed (vessel-charter contract model). Contract visibility:
  - **Agastya: 5-year charter** with ONGC (via HAL Offshore) — long visibility.
  - Mix of **long-term + short-term** charters across the fleet → "steady revenue visibility."
  - Seamec III sailed 25-Dec-2025 for **Phase-2 Pipeline Replacement Project + DSF II** projects.
  - Completed turnkey revamping of **ONGC's NLM9 platform** ahead of schedule (Q3).
- **₹1,000 cr MoU with DG Shipping** (vessel acquisition commitment over next 2–3 years; one or more vessels; funding case-by-case — internal accrual or mix).
- **OALP-VIII:** ONGC won 7 of 10 blocks → exploration-positive, but **commercialization 4–6 years out**; no immediate tender upside for Seamec.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline (charters / EPC)

outlook.body:
- **Fleet expansion:** Swordfish (full year FY27), Agastya (live), Anant (Q1 FY27), + ₹1,000 cr DG Shipping MoU for 1+ more vessels over 2–3 yrs.
- **ONGC / offshore capex tailwind:** India $100bn upstream push; refining 260→300 MMTPA; ONGC-RIL offshore-resource-sharing MoU; OALP-VIII (long-dated).
- **Inorganic + organic:** open to acquisitions; near-term growth from existing assets + Anant.
- **HAL Offshore migration:** future contracts to be bid into Seamec → captive pipeline transferring from parent.
- **Exports/overseas:** Dubai sub operating (currently a small drag); conscious effort to consolidate core and trim overseas losses.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

outlook.body:
- Grow and diversify the fleet - the Company purchased Vessel SEAMEC AGASTYA (erstwhile NPP Nusantara) during the year, taking fleet strength to 8 vessels comprising 6 MSVs, 1 Barge and 1 OSV
- Maximise asset utilisation and deployment days across the fleet, both in India and overseas
- Upgrade existing assets to expand addressable work - SEAMEC GLORIOUS barge upgraded to accommodate 250 personnel from the existing 100, by installation of additional lifeboats
- Extend into vessel operation and management services for third-party owners, exemplified by the March 2026 award for O&M of ONGC-owned vessels SAMUDRA SEVAK and SAMUDRA PRABHA
- Lock in long-term charter contracts with ONGC and international clients to secure multi-year deployment visibility
- Adopt a pre-emptive and pragmatic approach to geopolitical disruption as a core mitigating focal point for overseas deployment and drydock access
- Chairman states a vision of becoming a vibrant, diversified conglomerate while delivering reliable, distinguished services to the growing oil and gas industry
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company purchased Vessel SEAMEC AGASTYA (erstwhile Vessel NPP Nusantara), bringing total fleet strength to 8 vessels comprising 6 Multi Support Vessels, 1 Barge and 1 Offshore Support Vessel. SEAMEC AGASTYA completed its statutory drydock after takeover and commenced its ONGC charter (through HAL Offshore Limited) from January 2026, with the contract expected to be completed in 2029. The Company's Barge SEAMEC GLORIOUS was upgraded to accommodate 250 personnel from the existing 100 personnel by installation of additional lifeboats, and is engaged on a 150 day charter by L&T from November 2025. Drydocking was carried out on Vessel Sea Diamond and Vessel Agastya during the year, and SEAMEC III and SEAMEC PRINCESS are scheduled to undergo drydock in June and August 2026 respectively. The Company also extended its footprint into asset-light services, winning a contract in March 2026 for Hiring of Operation and Management Services for the ONGC owned vessels SAMUDRA SEVAK and SAMUDRA PRABHA for a period of 2 years. Entity-level expansion during the year included the incorporation of step-down subsidiary Searete India IFSC Private Limited on 16 April 2025, a 50:50 joint venture with Arete Shipping DMCC held through Seamec International FZE.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Offshore Support Vessel market growth attributed to growth of offshore oil and gas exploration, expansion of offshore drilling activities, increasing need for logistic and platform support, and development of deep water fields
- Growth in the 2026 to 2030 forecast period attributed to growth of offshore wind installations, increasing offshore maintenance activities and rising demand for advance support vessels and multi support vessels
- India energy demand and economic development poised to go hand in hand, resulting in likely greater demand for oil and gas in the coming years and making the sector attractive to new investors
- Government of India consistently pursuing effective exploration and utilization of the marine potential of a coastline over 7,500 kms
- In India more emphasis is given to Automation Underwater Vehicles (AUV) and Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROV), critical for underwater diving and pipeline insertion and maintenance in deep and ultra deep water
- Connected Oil and Gas market projected to grow at a CAGR of 8.2% over the forecast period 2026-2035, supported by IoT sensors, edge computing and AI-driven predictive analytics, on a baseline of moderate oil prices averaging USD 65 - USD 85 per barrel
- Adverse geopolitical situation is a concern and threat for overseas deployment and for availing drydock services - one vessel that had recently completed drydock in Dubai was stranded for almost four months
- Revenue growth driven by deployment of vessels for a higher number of days, acquisition of a new vessel and new charter-hire contracts entered during the year
- The Company is assessed under the Tonnage Tax Scheme, hence lower tax expenses as compared to normal tax rates
- SEAMEC PALADIN engaged with ONGC on a long term contract through HAL Offshore Limited, running till 2028
- SEAMEC AGASTYA commenced its ONGC charter (through HAL Offshore Limited) from January 2026, expected to be completed in 2029
- SEAMEC II on long term contract with ONGC till August 2026
- SEAMEC DIAMOND (OSV) engaged with ONGC on long term contract for 3 years through HAL Offshore Limited
- SEAMEC SWORDFISH commenced a two year charter with M/s Safeen Al Behar Limited Company, UAE in August 2025
- SEAMEC GLORIOUS barge engaged on a 150 day charter by L&T from November 2025
- SEAMEC III and SEAMEC PRINCESS engaged with various clients viz. M/s Mubarak Marine UAE, M/s A D Engineers, M/s G R Infrastructure Limited and L&T
- Contract awarded in March 2026 for Hiring of Operation and Management Services for ONGC owned vessels SAMUDRA SEVAK and SAMUDRA PRABHA for a period of 2 years
